nodes.summary: For a bounding sieve whose sifting primes have product $P$ and a natural number $R$, the level-$R$ set is the set of divisors $l$ of $P$ with $l \le R$.
nodes.title: Selberg level set

nodes.summary: For every bounding sieve and every natural number $R \ge 1$, the level-$R$ Selberg sum is at least $1$.
nodes.title: The Selberg level sum is at least one

nodes.summary:
For a bounding sieve whose sifting primes have product $P$, with multiplicative density function $
u$, and a natural number $R$, the level-$R$ Selberg sum is $G = \sum_{l \mid P,\ l \le R} g(l)$, where $g(l) = 
u(l) \prod_{p \mid l} (1 - 
u(p))^{-1}$, the product running over the primes $p$ dividing $l$.

nodes.title: Selberg level weights are bounded by one

nodes.title: Error bound for the Selberg level weights

nodes.summary: For a bounding sieve whose sifting primes have product $P$, with density function $\nu$, a natural number $R$ and a divisor $l$ of $P$, the level-$R$ Selberg weights $\lambda_d$ satisfy $\sum_{d \mid P,\ l \mid d} \nu(d)\,\lambda_d = y_l$, where $y_l$ is the normalized level-$R$ Selberg $y$-coefficient at $l$.
nodes.title: Inversion formula for the Selberg level weights

nodes.summary: For a bounding sieve whose sifting primes have product $P$, with density function $\nu$, and a natural number $R \ge 1$, let $\lambda_d$ be the level-$R$ Selberg weights and $\Lambda_d = \sum_{d_1, d_2 \mid d,\ \operatorname{lcm}(d_1, d_2) = d} \lambda_{d_1} \lambda_{d_2}$ their $\Lambda^2$ coefficients. Then $\sum_{d \mid P} \Lambda_d\,\nu(d) = 1/G$, where $G$ is the level-$R$ Selberg sum.
nodes.title: Main term of the Selberg level weights

nodes.summary: For a bounding sieve whose sifting primes have product $P$, with density function $\nu$, a natural number $R \ge 1$ and a divisor $d$ of $P$, the level-$R$ Selberg weight $\lambda_d$ at $d$ satisfies $|\nu(d)\,\lambda_d| \le 1$.
nodes.title: Weighted bound for the Selberg level weights

nodes.summary: For every bounding sieve and every natural number $R \ge 1$, the level-$R$ Selberg weight at $1$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: The Selberg level weight at one

nodes.summary: For every bounding sieve and all natural numbers $R$ and $d$, if the level-$R$ Selberg weight $\lambda_d$ at $d$ is nonzero, then $d \le R$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
